name: Olathe Public Schools
districtFact: Olathe Public Schools uses a staged opening: grades K–5, 6 and 9 attend the opening half day before the first full K–12 day, while Early Childhood begins on the following school day. Elementary families may also need a separate Specials calendar when OPS publishes one for the school year.

about.title: A Kansas City metro district with school-level planning needs
about.content: Olathe Public Schools is Kansas USD 233 and describes itself as the largest school district in the Kansas City metro. The official directory lists more than 29,000 students across 58 buildings, including 36 elementary schools, 10 middle schools and five high schools. The district calendar is the right source for systemwide attendance dates, but each building supplies conference appointment times and its own event calendar.

about.title: One opening sequence, three student groups
about.content: The first date in the annual PDF is not a universal full day. Olathe first brings in grades K–5, grade 6 and grade 9 for an orientation-style half day; all K–12 students attend a full day next; Early Childhood begins after that. This sequence is repeated in both reviewed school years and matters for transportation, care and work schedules.

about.title: District dates do not replace every Olathe calendar
about.content: The annual district PDF covers school-year dates, regular and half-day hours, reporting periods, finals and possible inclement-weather make-up dates. Elementary families may also need a separate Specials calendar when OPS publishes one. School performances, athletics, club meetings and building-specific events belong to school or activity calendars, which Olathe publishes separately.

calendarNotes: Use the official district PDF for districtwide dates and grade-level attendance rules. The opening half day applies only to grades K–5, 6 and 9; it is not the first attendance date for grades 7–8 or 10–12, and Early Childhood begins later. Conference windows identify the days on which buildings schedule meetings, but individual schools provide appointment times. The day after each conference half day is a conference day with no students, followed by a separate no-school day. March and April professional days may also be labeled as possible inclement-weather dates, so families should check the current calendar and district announcements before treating them as guaranteed days off. When OPS publishes an Elementary Specials calendar, use the file for the applicable school year rather than assuming an earlier rotation still applies. Spanish PDFs translate the same district schedule rather than creating different attendance tracks. Imported ICS dates are one-time copies and do not update when OPS revises a PDF or activates a make-up date.

planningTips.title: Planning with the Olathe calendar
content: Check the grade-specific opening sequence before arranging first-week transportation or care. Grades K–5, 6 and 9 attend the published half day; all K–12 students attend the next full day; Early Childhood starts on the following school day.

Treat the October and February conference windows as appointment periods, not as multiday closures. Buildings provide meeting times, while the annual PDF separately names the half day, the no-student conference day and the additional no-school day.
Keep the March and April possible inclement-weather dates flexible. They are printed as professional days, but the district may use them to recover weather-related instructional time.
If OPS publishes an Elementary Specials calendar for the school year, elementary families should use that file alongside the district calendar.
Use the live district and school calendars for changes, performances, athletics and building events. The annual PDF and this page focus on districtwide school-year planning.

districtFaqs.q: Is the first date on the Olathe Public Schools calendar a full day for every student?
districtFaqs.a: No. Grades K–5, 6 and 9 attend a morning half day first. All K–12 students attend a full day on the next school day, and Early Childhood starts on the following school day.

districtFaqs.q: What does No EC mean on the Olathe calendar?
districtFaqs.a: EC means Early Childhood. When the PDF says No EC, Early Childhood students do not attend that date even if some or all K–12 grades do.

districtFaqs.q: Do Olathe conference dates mean students are out for the whole conference window?
districtFaqs.a: No. The window shows when buildings schedule conferences. The final student day in the window is a half day, the next published conference day has no students, and a separate no-school day follows. Schools provide appointment times.

districtFaqs.q: Can Olathe use a professional day as a weather make-up day?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. Each reviewed PDF names one March professional day and one April professional day as possible inclement-weather dates. Check OPS announcements before relying on those dates as days off.

districtFaqs.q: Are Olathe's Spanish calendars separate school schedules?
districtFaqs.a: No. They are official Spanish translations of the English district calendars and publish the same dates, reporting periods and school hours.

districtFaqs.q: Where should families look for Olathe school events and conference times?
districtFaqs.a: Use the child's school calendar for building events and the building's conference communication for appointment times. The district calendar page supplies systemwide dates and links to school calendars.

districtFaqs.q: How does Olathe announce weather closures or delays?
districtFaqs.a: OPS sends cancellation notices by text and email, posts them on district channels and local media, and updates its information line. The district says it posts when a cancellation occurs, not when school is proceeding normally.

customSections.label: Which Olathe Calendar Should a Family Use?
customSections.content: Olathe publishes several calendars because they answer different questions. Start with the district PDF, then add only the source needed for a child's grade or building.
